summary: The lecture explains the salient features of the Indian Constitution and their sources from various countries. It details borrowings from the Government of India Act 1935, UK, USA, Ireland, Canada, Australia, Germany, USSR, France, South Africa, and Japan. It then lists unique features of the Indian Constitution such as its length, single citizenship, universal adult franchise, independent judiciary, fundamental rights and duties, directive principles, federal with unitary bias, judicial review, and three-tier governance.
points: Government of India Act 1935: federal scheme, Governor, judiciary, PSC, emergency, administrative details.
UK: parliamentary government, single citizenship, rule of law, parliamentary procedures.
USA: Preamble, fundamental rights, judicial review, removal of President, SC/HC judges, VP.
Ireland: Directive Principles, President election, Rajya Sabha 12 nominations.
Canada: strong centre federation, residuary powers to centre, governor appointment by centre, SC advisory jurisdiction.
Australia: Concurrent list, Centre-State relations, trade freedom, joint sitting of Parliament.
Indian Constitution originally 395 articles, 22 parts, 8 schedules; now 465 articles, 25 parts, 12 schedules.
Single citizenship under Citizenship Act 1955, amended 8 times, latest Feb 27 2015.
Universal adult franchise at 18 years, reduced from 21 by 61st Amendment 1988.
Fundamental duties added by 42nd Amendment 1976 (Art 51A), originally 10 now 11.

check.q: Which country's constitution inspired the Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution?
By which amendment was the voting age reduced from 21 to 18 years in India?
Which amendment added Fundamental Duties to the Indian Constitution?
